title: Maximum Number of Points From Grid Queries
summary: Given an m x n grid and an array of queries, determine the maximum points you can collect for each query by moving to adjacent cells if the query value exceeds the current cell's value, starting from the top-left corner.
statement: Given an m x n grid and an array of queries, determine the maximum points you can collect for each query by moving to adjacent cells if the query value exceeds the current cell's value, starting from the top-left corner. Record the points for each query in the output array.
constraints: For each query, start at the top-left cell and visit four-directionally connected cells whose values are strictly less than the query.
Each visited cell contributes one point and may be used once for that query.
Return maximum point counts in original query order.
hints: Sort queries while retaining their original indexes.
Maintain a min-heap frontier from the top-left and permanently expand cells below the current threshold.
As thresholds increase, reuse the reached set and write its count to the saved query index.
The heap always exposes the smallest boundary cell; all and only cells below each threshold become reachable before that query is recorded.
editorial: The heap always exposes the smallest boundary cell; all and only cells below each threshold become reachable before that query is recorded.

tests.explanation: Thresholds five, six, and two reach five, eight, and one cells respectively.
A query equal to the start value reaches zero cells, while six reaches the one cell.
